question: Sarah's phone showed 148 minutes of battery remaining. During a video call, it drained by 27 minutes. Then gaming used 55 more minutes. After charging, she gained back 55 minutes. She then spent 33 minutes texting and 39 minutes reading. Her phone case cost $45. After the video call and gaming, how many minutes of battery remained?

Tom had 79 trading cards at the start. He doubled his collection by finding 79 more. Then he acquired 55 additional cards from a trade and 18 more from a purchase. Later, he gave away 120 cards. His friend had 200 cards but didn't trade. How many cards did Tom have after the trade but before the giveaway?

A chocolate factory started with 226 kilograms of cocoa. They processed it by multiplying the amount 6 times for large batches. Then they added 53 kilograms of new supply. They multiplied the entire amount 7 times over the week. Then they multiplied it 6 times more for seasonal production. The storage warehouse held 5000 kilograms. What was the weight after adding the new supply but before the weekly multiplications?

Alex started with 184 trading cards. He multiplied his collection 7 times through various trades. Then he multiplied again by 5 through online sales. His sister had 400 cards, which he didn't count. He multiplied his total by 8 in a final trading event. By 46 cards. How many cards did Alex have after the first two multiplications?

A farmer planted 121 seeds initially. He added 20 more seeds in the morning and 54 in the afternoon. He multiplied the total plantings 9 times by planting in rows. He then removed 663 diseased plants. Finally, he added back 64 healthy seeds and 68 more for backup. The field irrigation system cost $500. How many plants were there after multiplication but before removing the diseased ones?

Maria's bank account started with 71 dollars. She withdrew 53 dollars for groceries. She deposited 29 dollars from her paycheck. She withdrew 37 dollars for gas and 9 dollars for parking. Then she deposited 80 dollars. Finally, her account balance was multiplied by 9 due to an error correction in cents to dollars conversion. Her car insurance was 200 dollars. After all withdrawals and deposits but before the multiplication, what was her balance in dollars?

An orchard had 207 apple trees initially. They multiplied the count 6 times through planting expansion. Then they added 44 newly planted trees. They subtracted 697 trees due to land sale. They multiplied by 9 for a future projection calculation. They added 61 more saplings. The neighboring farm had 1000 trees but this was separate. After multiplication and before the land sale, how many trees did they have (express as a word quantity where appropriate)?

Ben had 82 dollars in his wallet. He found 53 dollars on the street. He then multiplied his money 6 times by winning a prize. In the morning he multiplied by 3 more through a bonus, then by 9 in the afternoon. Finally, he spent 20528 dollars. His monthly rent was 800 dollars. After finding the money but before the morning multiplication, how much did Ben have?

A gardener started with 102 seedlings. She removed 93 that didn't survive. She added 35 new saplings. She multiplied the healthy seedlings by 9 to plan for propagation. She added 12 more seeds. The store had 500 seeds in stock but she didn't purchase them. After addition but before multiplication, how many seedlings did she have?

Sarah began with 122 dollars in savings. She earned 42 dollars from her part-time job. Then her total was multiplied by 4 due to a bonus calculation error. She earned 69 more dollars. She spent 272 dollars on a bike. She earned another 79 dollars. A gaming console cost 300 dollars but she didn't buy it. After earning the 42 dollars but before multiplication, how much did she have?

Jamie started with 51 dollars. She earned 9 dollars from chores. Then she multiplied her money 4 times by winning a contest. Half of her earnings went to a college fund. She then divided by 4 more times for gift distribution. Finally she added 45 dollars from her grandma. The movie ticket cost 12 dollars but she already saw it. After chores in the morning, splitting her earnings in the afternoon, and receiving money in the evening, what was her final amount divided by what it was after the afternoon work?

Alex had 95 hours of free time. He spent 10 hours on homework and 69 hours on sleep. He added back 65 hours through vacation. He multiplied by 6 for a project deadline calculation. He added 41 more hours. The school year had 180 days but this didn't affect his time. After subtraction but before multiplication, how many hours of free time remained?

Mark started with 89 dollars. He doubled his money (multiplied by 2) through a found wallet. He added 52 dollars from his job. He subtracted 36 dollars for gas. He multiplied by 7 for a project estimate. He added 78 dollars. His car insurance cost 150 dollars monthly. After doubling and adding the 52, what was his total before spending on gas?

A savings account started with 191 dollars. They withdrew 180 dollars. They added 62 dollars. They doubled the balance (multiplied by 2). They subtracted 98 dollars in fees. They added 45 dollars in interest (converting dollars to cents). By afternoon, he had earned 50 dollars more in other accounts. After withdrawal and adding 62, how much remained?

A baker started with 232 cookies. They removed 132 cookies for a sale. They multiplied the remaining by 6 for a batch estimate. They divided by half through packaging. They divided by 5 more times for smaller portions. Finally they subtracted 18 for samples. In the morning, during the day—what was the amount after removing the initial cookies and multiplying but before dividing?

A gym had 106 members. They removed 60 members who cancelled. They tripled membership through recruitment (multiplied by 3). They divided by half for facility planning. They subtracted 38 more cancellations. A rival gym had 200 members but this didn't affect their count. After removing the initial members but before tripling, how many remained?

A cafe started with 28 customers. They subtracted 19 who left early. They added 26 returning customers. They added 51 new customers. They added 63 during the evening rush. Two nearby cafes had 40 customers each combined. After the morning departure, adding afternoon customers step-by-step—how many after adding the first 26?

A student had 39 dollars. They added 80 dollars from their paycheck. They added 33 dollars from a gift. They divided by half for splitting savings. They tripled by 3 for investment multiplying. They added 42 more dollars. Their textbook cost 200 dollars but they didn't buy it today. After adding the paycheck and gift, but before dividing, how much did they have?

A baker had 89 loaves. They added 74 loaves in the morning rush. They subtracted 130 loaves sold by mid-day. They subtracted 24 more due to expiration. They added 11 back from a return (converting to a unit change if minutes to hours mattered). A competitor made 200 loaves. After adding the morning batch but before subtracting sales, how many loaves?

A store had 151 items. They multiplied by 5 for inventory expansion. They added 76 items. They added 66 more items. They subtracted 862 for a large order. They multiplied by 7 for shipment calculations (and measured time in hours for delivery). The warehouse had capacity for 2000 items. After multiplying by 5, then adding both shipments, how many items before the large order?

A photographer had 199 photos. They doubled the count (multiplied by 2) through digital enhancement. They added 63 more photos from a shoot. They multiplied by 6 for batch processing. They added 45 photos for album finalization. A competitor had 500 photos but didn't contribute. Using a word quantity, twice her original amount—how many photos after doubling and adding the shoot, but before multiplication?

A warehouse started with 128 items. They subtracted 10 for quality checks. They added 40 items from restocking. They divided by half for package counting. They added 55 items. They added 28 more. In the morning, afternoon, then evening—they multiplied by 9 for regional projections. After adding then dividing, how many items existed before the final multiplication?

A baker started with 59 loaves. They added 78 loaves in the morning. They multiplied by 9 for planning. They added 68 more loaves. They multiplied by 5 for shipment projections. A competitor's oven made 400 loaves but was unrelated. After adding the morning batch but before the first multiplication, how many loaves?

A student had 60 dollars. They doubled it (multiplied by 2). They subtracted 107 dollars in expenses. They added 51 dollars from work. They multiplied by 4 for tax calculation (minutes to hours conversion for work tracking). A scholarship was worth 500 dollars but separate. After doubling but before expense subtraction, how much?

A library had 110 books. They divided by half for classification. They subtracted 1 for a damaged book. They multiplied by 7 for shelf projections. They added 80 books from a donation. They added 19 more books. The annex had 250 books separately. After dividing and subtracting but before multiplication, how many books?
